key_insight: Introducing a post-training reinforcement method that uses super-linear advantage shaping to prevent reward hacking in text-to-image models: amplifying true improvements while removing miscalibrating normalization yields more genuine performance gains.
problem_solved: Existing GRPO-style post-training methods exploit biases in imperfect reward functions (reward hacking) because prompt-level normalization miscalibrates advantages, so models optimize surrogate artifacts instead of real image quality or alignment.
method: Diagnose miscalibration from prompt-level normalization and remove or correct the normalization step that flattens across-prompt signal.
Apply a super-linear advantage shaping transform (e.g., power function with exponent >1) to amplify meaningful advantages and suppress small noisy signals that drive reward hacking.
Integrate the shaped advantages into a GRPO-compatible post-training loop with regularization to retain diversity and stability.
impact: Makes post-training RL for T2I models more robust: practitioners get measurable, real improvements in image quality and alignment with fewer failure modes from reward-function artifacts, while retaining compatibility with existing GRPO pipelines.
visual_elements: Curve plot comparing linear vs. super-linear advantage transforms (showing amplification of large advantages and attenuation of small ones).
Before/after image grid illustrating reduced reward-hacked artifacts vs. genuinely improved samples.
Training-flow diagram: reward → advantage computation (old vs. new) → GRPO update → validation metrics.
Bar chart or table summarizing reductions in reward-hacking metrics and gains in human-preference or FID-style scores.
paper_title: Power Reinforcement Post-Training of Text-to-Image Models with Super-Linear Advantage Shaping
paper_authors: Haoyuan Sun, Jing Wang, Yuxin Song, Yu Lu, Bo Fang
